bigPicture: The AI stack is being rebuilt around agents as infrastructure — not as demos — with Cloudflare, OpenAI, and open-source models all racing to become the default plumbing, while compute scarcity looms as the constraint nobody's pricing in.

dataPoints.stat: Open-source 3B-parameter model matches frontier coding performance
dataPoints.context: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, 3B active params) rivals Claude Opus on coding tasks per Simon Willison's tests — 1,196 HN upvotes signal massive builder interest in local-first AI

dataPoints.stat: Claude Opus 4.7 launch hits 1,874 HN upvotes — highest signal item of the day
dataPoints.context: Anthropic's accelerating release cadence (Opus 4.7 + Mythos preview) shows the frontier model race is now measured in weeks, not quarters

dataPoints.stat: Cloudflare launched 2 agent primitives in one cycle: inference layer + programmatic email
dataPoints.context: Combined 746 HN upvotes — infra players are betting agents need dedicated plumbing, not just API wrappers

dataPoints.stat: OpenAI's Codex expands beyond code into general agentic tasks
dataPoints.context: Direct assault on Claude Code's positioning — the agentic coding market is now a three-way race (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source local)

tldr: Agent infrastructure is the new battleground: Cloudflare (inference + email), OpenAI (Agents SDK + Codex expansion), and git-native artifact storage all signal that 2025's agent demos are becoming 2026's production plumbing.
Open-source models just crossed the 'good enough' line for agentic coding — Qwen's 3B active-param MoE running locally challenges the economics of paying for frontier API calls.
Frontier model releases are accelerating to weeks-not-quarters cadence: Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-Rosalind (vertical bio), Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS — specialization and speed are the new moats.
Compute scarcity is the elephant in the room: Jensen Huang on supply chain moats + 'The Beginning of Scarcity in AI' signal that infinite-scale assumptions will break in 2026.

Contrarian undercurrent gaining traction: AI cybersecurity lacks verifiability (antirez), human-in-the-loop is theater at machine speed, and independent researchers are replicating safety claims themselves — trust infrastructure matters as much as capability.
